Package io.mdudel.zenoh.purejava

Enum Class TopicSource

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Enum<TopicSource>
io.mdudel.zenoh.purejava.TopicSource
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Comparable<TopicSource>, Constable
public enum TopicSource extends Enum<TopicSource>
How a topic came to be known to a TopicRegistry.

Zenoh has no topic registry of its own, so there is no single authoritative answer to "what topics exist". Each source below observes a different, partially-overlapping slice of the network, and each has a different failure mode. A TopicInfo therefore carries the set of sources that saw it, so callers can judge how much to trust an entry rather than being handed an undifferentiated list of strings.

  • Enum Constant Details

    • DECLARED_SUBSCRIBER

      public static final TopicSource DECLARED_SUBSCRIBER
      Some peer has declared a subscription matching this key.

      Tells you someone is listening. It does NOT tell you anyone is publishing. A key with an active publisher and no subscribers is invisible to this source.

    • DECLARED_QUERYABLE

      public static final TopicSource DECLARED_QUERYABLE
      Some peer has declared a queryable on this key, meaning it answers queries there.

      This client cannot itself issue queries, because Request and Response messages are not implemented, but it can still observe that queryables exist.

    • LIVENESS_TOKEN

      public static final TopicSource LIVENESS_TOKEN
      Some peer holds a liveliness token on this key.

      The highest-confidence source. A token is an explicit assertion of "I am alive at this key", and the router withdraws it automatically when the holder's session drops. Unlike the other declaration sources it reflects deliberate intent rather than an inference, but it only works for applications that bother to declare tokens.

    • OBSERVED_TRAFFIC

      public static final TopicSource OBSERVED_TRAFFIC
      A message was actually received on this key during the observation window.

      The only source that proves data is really flowing. Its weakness is the mirror image of the declaration sources: a topic that stays silent for the whole window never appears, however busy it may be at other times. It also requires permission to subscribe to the pattern being watched, which an ACL may refuse.
